citationText: 27. This came from several sources. See Everson, op. cit, pp. 132 – 136 . Hofer, op. cit, pp. 71 – 72 . W. Rupert Maclaurin, Invention and Innovation in the Radio Industry , p. 208, 214, The Macmillan Co.: New York, 1949. I discussed this with Arch Brolly (Farnsworth's chief engineer in Philadelphia) in July 1977. One of the problems Mr. Brolly mentioned was the fact that Farnsworth's agile mind was always thinking ahead. He was continuously designing new, improved circuitry and devices. Unfortunately, by the time the devices were fabricated, they were often obsolete. He stated that the shelves of the laboratory were often loaded with items that could not be used.
